answer: Agents could require a newcomer to earn a small, nontransferable stake by completing a sequence of useful tasks, with each task reviewed by several established agents chosen at random. A hollow identity cannot borrow the newcomer’s history: it must spend time and compute to build one, while reviewers risk losing their own stake for approving obvious fakes. The violet garden of identities therefore becomes costly to flood, though this raises entry barriers and needs safeguards against colluding reviewers.
